name: PBB Support System
shortDescription: A designated support-node workbench for consolidating SITREPs and managing inter-node support requests.
longDescription: PBB Support System / Imperium receives Relay-delivered situation reports and support requests at a designated support node. It stages the latest valid report from each source, prepares a consolidated current picture, and gives support operators a controlled request lifecycle.

Imperium also receives Relay source-heartbeat operational webhooks and can publish accepted snapshots through PBB Realtime. Its placement, users, credentials, retention rules, and receiving-agency authority remain deployment-specific.

readiness.note: SITREP intake and consolidation, support-request handling, Relay delivery, source-heartbeat webhooks, Realtime publishing, and map context are implemented.
remainingWork: Confirm operational placement and receiving-agency authority.
Harden role enforcement and remove development credentials.
Publish token ownership, retention, and multi-node operating runbooks.

problemSolved: Local emergency nodes need a structured way to request outside help and give receiving agencies a consolidated, current view without copying every editable incident record across the network.

workflowSteps.title: Receive selected reports
workflowSteps.description: Relay delivers validated SITREPs, support requests, and operational source-heartbeat events to the designated node.

workflowSteps.title: Consolidate current context
workflowSteps.description: Imperium stages the latest valid SITREP per source and builds a current support-level picture.

workflowSteps.title: Coordinate support
workflowSteps.description: Operators review, accept, reject, assign, track, and fulfill support requests through a local lifecycle.

workflowSteps.title: Send selected updates
workflowSteps.description: Consolidated SITREPs and request lifecycle events enter Relay-backed delivery when the route is reachable.

localCapabilities: Staged SITREPs, consolidation, request review, operator actions, and local history remain available from the support database.
Prepared map context can remain available from the local MapServer cache.
requiresLocalServices: The Laravel application, MySQL, queue worker, and scheduler support the confirmed workflows.
Relay is required for new cross-node intake and outbound lifecycle delivery; MapServer and Realtime support their configured views.
syncsWhenConnected: Relay can deliver new source SITREPs and Hotline support requests.
Imperium can submit consolidated SITREPs and supported lifecycle updates through Relay.
connectivityRequired: Cross-node delivery depends on a reachable Relay route and configured topology.
Remote evidence access requires a separately configured and authorized Hotline media endpoint.
notSynchronized: Imperium does not create universal database replication between nodes.
Editable Hotline incidents are not copied into a shared mutable incident database.

faqs.question: Where should Imperium be deployed?
faqs.answer: Imperium should run on an approved support or command node. The deployment owner decides whether that node belongs to a city, municipality, province, agency, or PBB headquarters.

faqs.question: Does it copy every Hotline incident?
faqs.answer: No. Imperium receives selected situation reports and support requests, not full editable copies of every Hotline incident.

faqs.question: What remains available when upstream connectivity is lost?
faqs.answer: Reports already received, the combined situation view, local support requests, and local history remain available while the node services are running.

faqs.question: How are source heartbeats received?
faqs.answer: Relay sends a separate status update that tells Imperium whether a reporting source is still active. These health updates are kept separate from ordinary reports and requests.

faqs.question: Will the support map work offline?
faqs.answer: Only map areas and boundaries prepared in advance will work reliably offline. Looking outside those prepared areas may require an online map source.

faqs.question: Is Imperium ready for unrestricted agency access?
faqs.answer: No. Before agencies share it, the deployment owner must strengthen and approve user roles, sign-in credentials, who may receive requests, how long records are kept, and the operating procedures.
